fit: single versus 10-day oral ethanol extract and forced-swim duration in rats
assessment: The single-dose groups showed no clear immobility effect. The ten-day extract comparisons favored shorter immobility at higher doses in males and at all assessed doses in females, and fluoxetine showed a larger effect. The forced-swim sex-by-treatment test was not significant. No clinical Parkinson or brewed-tea condition.

fit: concentrated water extract and separate rosmarinic acid control in rats
assessment: The short experiment found shorter swim immobility with extract and isolated rosmarinic acid, while swimming and struggling did not clearly change. Ten-day extract groups had less immobility and more swimming. The freeze-dried 12% rosmarinic acid extract, animal assay and absence of clinical outcomes limit transfer.

fit: single dry extract and two defined mixtures in a chronic-stress rat model
assessment: Forced-swim immobility with Melissa alone was 199.0 versus 225.5 seconds in stressed controls, p=.348. The Melissa-containing blend was also inconclusive. The other blend showed a favorable comparison and contained no Melissa. The study uses small animal groups and no brewed or Parkinson exposure.

fit: lemon-balm infusion and pooled self-reported symptom changes in psychiatric patients
assessment: Of 26 lemon-balm users, 11 used it with prescribed treatment. Seven reported no change and three decreased intensity. The remaining co-user has no reported direction. The herb row lists dizziness and nausea. Changes are pooled across symptoms and cannot be attributed to the herb or to depression separately.

fit: lemon-balm infusion in a separate psychotic outpatient survey
assessment: Fifteen used lemon balm, two naming depression as the indication. Among eight co-users with medication, five reported no change and three reduced symptoms. One nausea report is listed. The outcomes are pooled across symptoms and are separate from the non-psychotic cohort.

fit: oral hydroalcoholic concentrate in restraint-stressed mice
assessment: Middle and highest groups showed lower swim and suspension immobility than restraint controls. Open-field locomotion was not clearly changed. Methods and Results label the middle arm 75 mg/kg while an accepted figure caption prints 100 mg/kg. Neither a brewed infusion nor a human depression outcome was tested.

fit: individual dry extract and mixture effects on rat serum cytokines
assessment: Both blends reduced chronic TNF-α and IL-6 in the stress model, while single Melissa showed no clear chronic cytokine change. The 2017 behavioral report shares project and formulation details. Cohort overlap is unresolved and this assay does not show a depression effect.

fit: injected hydroalcoholic extract and opposing sucrose preference outcomes by diet
assessment: Sucrose intake increased relative to high-fat diet vehicle controls. The lowest extract dose decreased sucrose preference under normal diet versus its own vehicle. Both directions are tied to diet-specific controls and an injection route in rats, with no oral tea or clinical depressive symptoms.

fit: traditional dried-leaf tea use and reported indications in Niš district
assessment: Fourteen of 100 surveyed community participants reported lemon-balm use. The original table records dried-leaf tea and one report lists depression among intended uses. The survey supplied neither symptom trajectories nor a Parkinson cohort.
